newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 27.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
EX-PRIME MINISTER CHARGESHEETED IN ST KITT'S CASE

The Central Bureau of Investigation has charged former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in the St Kitts forgery case. The charge-sheet came soon after the Delhi High Court rejected his anticipatory bail plea in the Lakhubhai cheating case. The charge-sheet says Rao, during his stint as the Foreign Minister in the Rajiv Gandhi Government in 1986, had conspired with Chandraswami to tarnish the reputation of V.P. Singh, who later he became the prime minister.
Financial Express
UK POWER GIANT SEEKS MORE INDIAN JOINT VENTURES

British power major Eastern Generation (EG) plans to invest around $500-million in the Indian power sector over the next five years. The company has already bid for six power projects in Gujarat. It is shifting its focus to investment opportunities in this sector in Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and Kerala. EG, which has a global turnover of $1.5 billion, is scouting for domestic power companies to form joint ventures in India. For the Gujarat projects, EG has floated a 50:50 joint venture with Gujarat Gas Company.
SIEMENS MAY TIE UP WITH CESC LTD FOR POWER PROJECT

Germany's Siemens AG is poised to replace UK's Rolls Royce Power Generation as the engineering and procurement contractor for the CESC Ltd promoted Balagarh Power Company. The 22.35 billion rupee project is a joint venture between CESC and Rolls Royce. The 1,500 megawatt coal-based Balagarh power company is being set up in three phases of 500 megawatt units each. The Indian equity in the thermal power plant is worth two billion rupees. The overseas stake is pegged at $113 million. Of this, Rolls Royce holding is roughly $43 million.
RELIANCE CAPITAL PLANS TO GO FOR $100 MLN ECBS

Reliance group flagship Reliance Capital plans to raise $100 million through external commercial borrowings (ECB) soon. The non-banking financial company is also talking with banks for a network arrangement for its fixed deposit programme for 1996/97 (April-March). Reliance Capital's $100-million ECB will have a maturity period of seven years. Sources said the ECB will be priced anywhere between 100 to 200 basis points over Libor.
40 STATE UNITS REFERRED TO DISINVESTMENT COMMISSION

The Core Group on Divestment has referred 40 profit-making public sector undertakings (PSUs) to the Disinvestment Commission for formulating restructuring and divestment packages. The PSUs include Hindalco, Nalco, Batco, ITI, ITDC, Air India, SAIL, FAIL, Hindustan Zinc, Power Grid Corp of India, Shipping Corp of India and others. Disinvestment plans to consider the Core Group's reference on October 10.
The Economic Times
TATAS SCRAP PLAN FOR STAINLESS STEEL PLANT IN ORISSA

Tata flagship Tisco has scrapped its plan to set up a stainless steel plant in Orissa and shelve expansion plans at its chrome conversion unit in Bamnipal. The decision was taken in view of the recent huge cut-back in its chrome mining land in the Sukinda Valley, Orissa. Tisco's present mining land is about 406 hectares, too small to provide the raw material for setting up a stainless unit of minimum economic size. International stainless steel majors like Ottokumpo of Finland and Nippon Steel of Japan were negotiating with Tisco for a possible joint venture near Bamnipal in Orissa.
COGENTRIX LIKELY TO GET COUNTER-GUARANTEE

The government may provide a counter-guarantee to the Cogentrix power project. However, the Karnataka State Electricity Board (KSEB) is yet to achieve the stipulated three percent rate of return (ROR) on its net assets. The government has made it mandatory for SEBs seeking counter-guarantees from the Centre to achieve three percent ROR. KSEB has failed to meet this minimum requirement despite a recent tariff hike of 31 percent. The government had made an assurance that counter-gurantees for the fast-track projects would be issued by the end of September.
OIL MINISTRY FINALISING ADMINISTERED PRICING PHASE-OUT NOTE

The Petroleum Ministry proposes to replace the administered pricing mechanism with market-based pricing and distribution system. To begin with, tariff structure would be rationalised, retention merging concept for refineries withdrawn and the marketing sector partially deregulated. The ministry has circulated a cabinet note for a new exploration licensing policy. The ministry also plans to move the cabinet for offering small-sized oil fields and exploration blocks to the private sector.
Business Standard
OIL MAJOR'S CRUDE OUTPUT TO PLUNGE

The Oil and Natural Gas Corp's (ONGC) production is expected to drop by 2.5 million tonnes in the current financial year. This is being considered a major setback to the country's crude oil production programme. ONGC's low level of production is expected to continue during the next financial year as well because of the rectification measures being undertaken in many of ONGC's oilfields. At the current international crude oil price of $22 a barrel, this drop in production will mean an additional annual oil import bill of $385 million.
GRASIM INDUSTRIES THIRD LARGEST CEMENT PRODUCER

Grasim Industries has emerged as the country's third largest cement producer after Associated Cement Companies (ACC) and Larsen & Toubro (L&T). The Aditya Birla group flagship has already expanded capacity of its Raipur plant from one million tonnes to 1.5 million tonnes by adding 500,000 tonnes of slag cement. This has taken Grasim's overall capacity from 4.5 million tonnes to five million tonnes. L&T has a six million tonne capacity, while ACC has a capacity of 10 million tonnes.
MOBILINK PLANS TO EXPAND REACH

Mobilink, the Dalmiya-Sunkyong-Samsung-owned paging telecommunication network, is planning to enter into a series of strategic alliances with various network operators. The company's move is aimed at extending its operations to a total of 50 major cities in the country. At present, Mobilink offers its multi-city services to 10 major cities and has a project investment of over one billin rupees.
The Observer
THREE NATIONALISED BANKS TO GO PUBLIC

Three nationalised banks, Banks of India (BOI), Canara Bank and Corporation Bank, are set to hit the stock market with massive public issues. These banks are expecting favourable response from foreign institutional investors (FIIs). Sources said BOI plans to float public issue in the next two months as it has no plans to go in for Global Depository Receipt issue in the near future. Priced between 50 to 60 rupees, the issues would mostly be picked up by the FIIs, who have given assurance to the bank in this regard. BOI plans to sell off nearly 30 percent of its equity.
Business Line
WHEAT PRODUCT EXPORTS MAY BE SUSPENDED

The government plans to suspend wheat product exports to ease the mounting pressure on domestic prices. The proposal to block export of value added wheat products was mooted by the Food Ministry, sources said. So far free export of value-added wheat products has been allowed. The proposed move comes in the wake of mounting pressure to augment domestic supplies. It also comes close on the heels of the government's decision to halve the ceiling on export of wheat from three million tonnes to 1.5 million tonnes during the current fiscal.
